coverage: A connected review of static and fully dynamic problems, not a complete survey. Published algorithms and elementary baselines are distinguished; no best-known frontier is claimed.

nodes.label: All-pairs shortest paths
nodes.contract: Directed n-vertex graphs; polynomially bounded integer weights; no negative cycles. Output all pairwise distances.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; O(log n)-bit word RAM for the displayed integer preprints.

baselines.detail: Floyd–Warshall baseline; not a best-known claim.

lower.detail: The classical conditional premise is retained for interpreting reductions. October 2026 preprints claim polynomial improvements; this is not shown as an established current barrier.

claims.detail: Conservative exponent from the abstract; deterministic polynomial-size integer weights. Theorem inspected; proof not independently verified.
Deterministic, polynomial-size integer weights. Separate follow-up preprint claim; not a referee assessment.

nodes.label: Min-plus matrix product
nodes.contract: Two n×n integer matrices with polynomially bounded entries; Cᵢⱼ = minₖ(Aᵢₖ+Bₖⱼ).
nodes.parameter: n is matrix dimension, not the n²-entry input length.

baselines.detail: Direct product baseline; each output entry examines n candidates.

lower.detail: Subcubic equivalence is established. The old hypothesis is under review following the displayed 2026 claims.

claims.detail: Conservative stated exponent; deterministic word RAM, polynomially bounded integer entries.
Follow-up preprint claim for min-plus product; no independent proof verification here.

nodes.label: Negative triangle
nodes.contract: Weighted tripartite graph on n vertices. Decide whether some triangle has total weight strictly below zero; polynomially bounded integer weights.
nodes.parameter: n vertices. A negative triangle differs from a prescribed-weight or zero-weight triangle.

baselines.detail: Enumerate vertex triples; historical baseline.

lower.detail: Classical subcubic equivalence. Faster min-plus also gives faster negative-triangle detection; the preprint status is not silently promoted to a proved frontier.

nodes.label: Boolean matrix multiplication
nodes.contract: Compute the Boolean product of two n×n Boolean matrices.
nodes.parameter: n is matrix dimension. ω denotes the algebraic matrix multiplication exponent.

baselines.detail: Elementary triple-loop baseline.
Algebraic algorithms are already truly subcubic; no unrestricted cubic barrier is asserted.

lower.detail: A model-specific conjecture, not a lower bound for algebraic algorithms. ‘Combinatorial’ is a research convention, not a universal machine model.

nodes.label: Triangle detection
nodes.contract: Unweighted n-vertex graph; decide whether any triangle exists.
nodes.parameter: Vertex-based n. Detection does not mean listing all triangles or per-edge reporting.

baselines.detail: Square the adjacency matrix and inspect adjacent pairs; algebraic baseline.

lower.detail: Only the combinatorial conditional implication is shown. Algebraic subcubic algorithms are known.

nodes.label: CNF satisfiability
nodes.contract: Satisfiability with v variables and M clauses. SETH quantifies over clause widths: for every fixed saving, some width k resists that saving.
nodes.parameter: Exponential scale in v. It is not a polynomial n² or n³ problem.

baselines.detail: Exhaustive assignment baseline; not the best algorithm for every fixed clause width.

lower.detail: For every δ>0 there exists a width k with no deterministic O(2^{(1−δ)v}) algorithm up to polynomial factors. Randomized consequences require randomized SETH.

nodes.label: Orthogonal Vectors
nodes.contract: Two sets of N Boolean d-vectors. Is there a cross-pair with dot product zero?
nodes.parameter: N vectors per side; d=c log N in the fine-grained hardness regime, with c dependent on the desired exponent saving.

baselines.detail: Examine all cross-pairs.

lower.detail: Keep quantifiers over dimension and the desired saving. A randomized algorithm is ruled out only under the corresponding randomized hypothesis.

nodes.label: Exact graph diameter
nodes.contract: Connected, undirected, unweighted graph. Diameter D=maxᵤᵥ dist(u,v). Hardness already distinguishes D=2 from D=3.
nodes.parameter: n vertices, m edges; the explicit OV construction has m=Õ(n), not necessarily O(n).

baselines.detail: Run BFS from each vertex; Õ(n²) on m=Õ(n) instances.

lower.detail: For every fixed positive exponent saving. This is a conditional time bound for exact diameter. This barrier concerns deterministic algorithms; bounded-error randomized exclusions require randomized SETH/OVH.

nodes.label: Diameter below factor 3/2
nodes.contract: Connected, undirected, unweighted graph. Estimate D̂ with D/α≤D̂≤D for fixed α<3/2.
nodes.parameter: n vertices, m=Õ(n) in the explicit reduction. Fixed gap below 3/2 is essential.

baselines.detail: Exact BFS baseline meets this stricter approximation contract. The faster floor(2D/3) algorithm is a separate related guarantee below.

lower.detail: The D=2 versus D=3 gap excludes every fixed α<3/2. It does not exclude factor 3/2 or guarantees with additive rounding. This barrier concerns deterministic algorithms; bounded-error randomized exclusions require randomized SETH/OVH.

related.detail: ⌊2D/3⌋ ≤ D̂ ≤ D. The floor matters; this is not the same contract as a strict factor below 3/2.

nodes.label: Longest common subsequence
nodes.contract: Exact LCS length of two binary strings of length at most L.
nodes.parameter: L is string length. The reduction produces length O(Nd).

baselines.detail: Dynamic-programming baseline for equal-length strings; unequal lengths cost O(L₁L₂).

lower.detail: Already binary alphabets; exact LCS. Does not assert approximate-LCS hardness. This barrier concerns deterministic algorithms; bounded-error randomized exclusions require randomized SETH/OVH.

nodes.label: Edit distance
nodes.contract: Exact Levenshtein distance on two binary strings: unit-cost insertion, deletion and substitution.
nodes.parameter: L is maximum string length. Approximation and other cost choices require separate contracts.

baselines.detail: Dynamic-programming baseline.

lower.detail: Exact unit-cost edit distance on binary strings. Randomized bounds require a corresponding randomized hypothesis.

nodes.label: Integer 3SUM
nodes.contract: Given N polynomial-size integers, decide whether three distinct input positions sum to zero.
nodes.parameter: N integers; bit length and RAM model must be preserved.

baselines.detail: Sort and use two pointers; baseline rather than a best-known claim.

lower.detail: The randomized premise used by the triangle-listing reduction is historical in light of the October 2026 improvement claims.

claims.detail: Deterministic algorithm claimed for polynomial-size integers; full theorem checked, proof not independently verified.
Follow-up preprint claim; no independent proof verification here.

nodes.label: Triangle listing up to m outputs
nodes.contract: Unweighted tripartite m-edge graph. Report up to m distinct triangles, or all triangles if fewer exist.
nodes.parameter: m edges, not n vertices. The cap on output size is part of the problem.

baselines.detail: Chiba–Nishizeki gives O(m·a(G)) triangle listing; a(G)=O(√m). Input scanning/isolated vertices cost O(n).

lower.detail: Pătraşcu's conditional implication is for listing, not ordinary detection. It yields some positive saving in expected 3SUM time; no exact δ formula is assigned.

nodes.label: Online Boolean matrix-vector multiplication
nodes.contract: An N×N Boolean matrix is followed by N Boolean vectors, one at a time. Output the Boolean vector Mv before the next input arrives.
nodes.parameter: N is matrix dimension and number of vectors. Total time includes preprocessing in the original conjecture; derived hardness also permits polynomial matrix preprocessing.

baselines.detail: Direct Boolean products, including input reading.
Randomized total-time algorithm; the saving is not a fixed polynomial exponent.

lower.detail: For every fixed ε>0, the conjecture excludes bounded-error randomized algorithms (error at most 1/3). This is ordinary Boolean OMv, not a hinted or rectangular-hinted conjecture.

nodes.label: Online Boolean vector-matrix-vector multiplication
nodes.contract: Preprocess a Boolean a×b matrix. For each of T sequential vector pairs (u,v), output the Boolean scalar uᵀMv before the next pair. Fix a=floor(b^γ) for constant γ>0.
nodes.parameter: Square reference a=b=T=N for the displayed time bounds. Rectangular parameters used by reductions are stated on each arrow.

baselines.detail: General direct computation takes O(abT) online time after reading the matrix.

lower.detail: Theorem 2.7 rules out the paper’s polynomially sub-abT online computation for every fixed aspect exponent γ, with polynomial preprocessing in a,b and error at most 1/3. The displayed N exponent is only the square specialization.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic s–t reachability
nodes.contract: Fixed vertices s,t in a directed unweighted graph. Maintain whether a directed path exists after each edge update.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: Randomized fixed-pair reachability, worst-case updates; polynomial preprocessing O(n^ω). Use a fixed set H={s,t} in the matrix-inverse reduction. The numerical exponent is the published guarantee, not a current optimality claim.
baselines.locator: Theorem 4.2; Corollary C.12 and Theorem C.16

baselines.detail: Search from s after each update. Dense reference O(n²). Store the answer after the search; O(1) lookup. This is an elementary recomputation construction, not a frontier result.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. In general m notation, Corollary 3.4 excludes U=O(m^{1/2−η}), Q=O(m^{1−δ}), for positive constants η,δ. The n form is the dense-scale specialization.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic exact s–t distance
nodes.contract: Fixed s,t in an undirected unweighted graph. Maintain the exact distance, with infinity for disconnected terminals.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: Randomized exact distance, high probability against adaptive updates; worst-case update guarantee. The directed unweighted algorithm also covers undirected graphs (encode each undirected edge by two arcs). Preprocessing Õ(h n^ω), with the theorem’s polynomial choice of h. It outputs the distance after every update.
Run BFS from s after each update. Dense reference O(n²). Store the answer after the search; O(1) lookup. This is an elementary recomputation construction, not a frontier result.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. In general m notation, Corollary 3.4 excludes U=O(m^{1/2−η}), Q=O(m^{1−δ}), for positive constants η,δ. The n form is the dense-scale specialization.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic s–t distance, α < 5/3
nodes.contract: Undirected unweighted graph, fixed s,t, and a fixed factor 1<α<5/3. Return d≤d̂≤αd; zero additive error.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: For any fixed ε>0, maintain a (1+ε) estimate. Full update bound O(n^{1.407} ε⁻² log(1/ε)); preprocessing O(n^ω ε⁻² log(1/ε)). Choose ε below the row’s fixed α−1. The proof computes the estimate during updates, allowing constant lookup.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. In general m notation, Corollary 3.4 excludes U=O(m^{1/2−η}), Q=O(m^{1−δ}), for positive constants η,δ. The n form is the dense-scale specialization.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic s–t distance, α < 3
nodes.contract: Undirected unweighted graph, fixed s,t, and a fixed factor 1<α<3. Return d≤d̂≤αd. The weaker red threshold applies throughout this larger approximation range.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: For any fixed ε>0, maintain a (1+ε) estimate. Full update bound O(n^{1.407} ε⁻² log(1/ε)); preprocessing O(n^ω ε⁻² log(1/ε)). Choose ε below the row’s fixed α−1. The proof computes the estimate during updates, allowing constant lookup.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. η,δ>0 are constants. The hard instances need not be dense; this is a barrier for an algorithm covering all n-vertex graphs.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic diameter, α < 2
nodes.contract: Undirected graph with weights in {0,1}. Return D/α≤D̂≤D for a fixed factor 1≤α<2, where D is diameter. Exact recomputation meets this one-sided convention.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: Recompute every source distance with 0–1 BFS, then take the maximum; dense reference O(n³). Store the diameter for O(1) lookup. Polynomial preprocessing; disconnected graphs may report infinity. This elementary baseline is not a frontier claim.
baselines.locator: Corollary 3.22 problem contract; elementary all-sources construction

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. η,δ>0 are constants. The hard instances need not be dense; this is a barrier for an algorithm covering all n-vertex graphs.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic arbitrary-pair reachability
nodes.contract: General directed graph. Query endpoints u,v are supplied at query time; answer whether u reaches v. This row does not explicitly output the whole transitive closure matrix.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: Randomized worst-case update and arbitrary-pair query guarantees from dynamic matrix inverse. Polynomial preprocessing O(n^ω). Numerical exponent from the published bound; no optimality claim.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. In general m notation, Corollary 3.4 excludes U=O(m^{1/2−η}), Q=O(m^{1−δ}), for positive constants η,δ. The n form is the dense-scale specialization. An arbitrary-pair oracle solves fixed s–t queries, so that lower bound transfers.

nodes.label: Fully dynamic distance oracle, α < 2
nodes.contract: Undirected unweighted graph. Arbitrary endpoints at query time; (1+ε)-approximate distances with fixed 0<ε<1. The oracle supports any pair, not only a stored fixed pair.
nodes.parameter: n vertices; m edges. The figure evaluates dense-scale upper bounds at m=Θ(n²), on algorithms covering general graphs with at most n² edges.

baselines.detail: Randomized, high probability against adaptive updates; worst-case update O(n^{1.788}) F(n,ε), preprocessing O(n^{2.585}) F(n,ε), where F=O(1/ε)^{√(2 log₍₁/ε₎ n)}. Query O(n^{0.45} ε⁻²). For fixed ε the extra update factor is subpolynomial, not merely polylogarithmic.

lower.detail: Fully dynamic single-edge insertions and deletions; polynomial preprocessing; randomized error at most 1/3 is allowed in the conditional exclusion. The lower bound excludes a fixed polynomial improvement, including amortized updates. An arbitrary-pair oracle includes the single-source 2-versus-4 distance problem. Use δ=1/2 in the density parameter of Corollary 3.8, then m=Θ(n²).

edges.consequence: Min-plus in O(n^{3−δ}) gives APSP in Õ(n^{3−δ}).
edges.transformation: O(log n) repeated min-plus squarings; path weights stay polynomially bounded.
edges.notes: No negative cycles. The same exponent saving is preserved up to logarithmic factors.

edges.consequence: APSP in O(n^{3−δ}) gives min-plus in O(n^{3−δ}+n²).
edges.transformation: Three-layer directed acyclic graph on 3n vertices encodes the two matrices.
edges.notes: The produced graph has no negative cycles.

edges.consequence: Negative Triangle in O(n^{3−δ}) gives min-plus in Õ(n^{3−δ/3}).
edges.transformation: O(n² T(n^{1/3}) log W); T(n)/n nondecreasing, integer output magnitude W polynomial in n.
edges.notes: The exact improvement is not the same δ. Integer magnitude enters through log W.

edges.consequence: Min-plus in O(n^{3−δ}) gives Negative Triangle in O(n^{3−δ}+n²).
edges.transformation: One min-plus product over two tripartite layers and O(n²) comparisons against the third edge weight.
edges.notes: Strictly negative total weight. Exact/zero-weight triangles are different problems.

edges.consequence: Triangle detection in O(n^{3−δ}) gives Boolean product in O(n^{3−δ/3}).
edges.transformation: Boolean specialization of O(n² T(n^{1/3})) with constant value range.
edges.notes: Deterministic and combinatorial reduction. Any cubic hardness claim applies only to combinatorial algorithms.

edges.consequence: Boolean product in O(n^{ω+o(1)}) gives triangle detection in O(n^{ω+o(1)}+n²).
edges.transformation: Square the Boolean adjacency matrix and test pairs that are adjacent in the input graph.
edges.notes: Works for ordinary unweighted detection; not an output-sensitive listing reduction.

edges.consequence: For 0<δ≤1, OV in O(N^{2−δ} poly(d)) gives SAT time 2^{(1−δ/2)v} poly(M).
edges.transformation: Split v variables into two halves: N=2^{v/2} partial assignments per side; d=M clause indicators.
edges.notes: The displayed δ range includes the 2^{v/2} construction cost. SETH width and dimension quantifiers matter. Deterministic SETH does not by itself exclude bounded-error randomized algorithms.

edges.consequence: Exact diameter in O(n^{2−η}) on these graphs gives truly subquadratic OV for d=c log N.
edges.transformation: Connected unweighted undirected graph: n=2N+d+2; m≤2Nd+2N+2d+1. OV YES iff diameter 3, NO iff 2.
edges.locator: Theorem 1; explicit construction in VVW Theorem 3.2
edges.notes: The reduction has Õ(N) edges for logarithmic d. This direct consequence has its own size accounting.

edges.consequence: An O(n^{2−η}) algorithm with fixed α<3/2 and D/α≤D̂≤D gives truly subquadratic OV.
edges.transformation: The same 2-versus-3 diameter gap: D=2 yields D̂≤2; D=3 yields D̂>2.
edges.notes: No claim for α=3/2 or for floor(2D/3) guarantees.

edges.consequence: LCS in O(L^{2−ε}) gives OV in O(Nd+(Nd)^{2−ε}).
edges.transformation: Two binary strings, length O(Nd), constructed in O(Nd) time.
edges.notes: For d=c log N, polynomial exponent savings transfer up to logarithmic factors.

edges.consequence: Exact edit distance in O(L^{2−ε}) gives OV in O(Nd+(Nd)^{2−ε}).
edges.transformation: Binary-string alignment gadgets; length and construction time O(Nd); unit edit costs.
edges.notes: No approximate-distance hardness is inferred.

edges.consequence: Listing up to m triangles in O(m^{4/3−ε}) gives expected strongly subquadratic 3SUM.
edges.transformation: Randomized fine-grained reduction with output-sensitive listing; some positive saving follows.
edges.notes: No 3SUM-to-ordinary-detection edge is justified by this theorem. The premise is historical; the reduction remains meaningful.

edges.consequence: A polynomial online saving for OuMv contradicts ordinary Boolean OMv.
edges.transformation: Theorem 2.7 transfers OMv hardness to every fixed aspect ratio a=floor(b^γ), allowing polynomial matrix preprocessing. No identical exponent saving is asserted.
edges.notes: Online answers must be returned before seeing the next input. The square displayed reference and rectangular reductions use different parameter substitutions.

edges.consequence: U(n)=O(n^{1−η}) and Q(n)=O(n^{2−δ}) would give truly subcubic square OuMv.
edges.transformation: Square K×K matrix, K pairs: s→L→R→t gadget has 2K+2 vertices and O(K²) edges. O(K²) changes plus K queries give O(K²U+KQ+K²) online time.
edges.notes: Matrix edges encode M; source/target edges encode u,v. Undo each pair’s updates. Polynomial preprocessing and bounded error are part of the reduction.

edges.consequence: The stated jointly faster updates and queries give truly subcubic square OuMv.
edges.transformation: Square K×K matrix, K pairs: n=Θ(K), O(K²) changes and K queries. Online time O(K²U(n)+KQ(n)+K²). Distances distinguish 3 from at least 5.
edges.notes: Fully dynamic undo operations support the amortized lower bound. Exact distance distinguishes the gap.

edges.consequence: U(n)=O(n^{1−η}), Q(n)=O(n^{2−δ}) with fixed α<5/3 gives truly subcubic square OuMv.
edges.transformation: Same square construction: n=Θ(K), O(K²) changes and K queries; d≤d̂≤αd distinguishes d=3 from d≥5.
edges.notes: Strict factor threshold and zero additive error. The more general source condition is 3α+β<5.

edges.consequence: U(n)=O(n^{1/2−η}), Q(n)=O(n^{1−δ}) with fixed α<3 contradicts OMv.
edges.transformation: Square K×K matrix, K pairs. Subdivision gives n=Θ(K²), O(K²) updates and K queries: O(nU(n)+√n Q(n)+n), below n^{3/2} if both improve polynomially.
edges.notes: Fix the approximation gap before constructing the graph. Hard instances are sparse; this is not a dense-instance-only claim.

edges.consequence: U(n)=O(n^{1/2−η}), Q(n)=O(n^{1−δ}) for α<2 contradicts ordinary OMv.
edges.transformation: Use a=K, b=K², T=K². The graph has n=Θ(K²) vertices; O(K⁴) updates and O(K³) queries give O(n²U(n)+n^{3/2}Q(n)+n²), compared with abT=Θ(n^{5/2}).
edges.notes: Rectangular OuMv follows from Theorem 2.7, not a hinted conjecture. These explicit dimensions avoid inconsistent aspect-ratio/pair-count labels in the source proof. Weights {0,1}; hard instances have O(n^{3/2}) edges.

edges.consequence: A faster arbitrary-pair oracle with the stated query budget also solves the fixed-pair reachability problem.
edges.transformation: Apply the same square OuMv gadget and ask the fixed terminal pair through the arbitrary-pair interface: O(K²U+KQ+K²) online time.
edges.notes: No Ω(n²) update claim is inferred from the number of entries in an explicit closure matrix.

edges.consequence: U(n)=O(n^{1−η}) and Q(n)=O(n^{1−δ}) for α<2 gives truly subcubic square OuMv.
edges.transformation: Square K×K matrix, K pairs: n=Θ(K), O(K²) changes and O(K²) queries; O(K²(U+Q)+K²) online time. Query the source-to-row vertices selected by u.
edges.notes: The oracle includes single-source queries. A factor below 2 distinguishes distances 2 and at least 4; polynomial preprocessing and fully dynamic amortization are explicit.

Online matrix products & fully dynamic graphs

dynamicView.queryPolicy: Row-specific query guarantees; only update time is plotted.
dynamicView.density: Dense-scale reference: upper bounds evaluated at m=Θ(n²). Algorithms cover all n-vertex graphs with at most n² edges; some lower-bound instances are sparse.
dynamicView.assumption: Ordinary Boolean OMv; polynomial preprocessing. Red excludes every fixed polynomial saving below its boundary, including amortized updates.
